classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a light year as distance, convert years into seconds and multiply by light speed; part c requires switching to distance divided by speed.

content.prompt: A light year is the distance light travels in a year. Light travels at approximately $3\times10^5$ km/s. Use 1 year = 365 days.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How wide is our galaxy (in kilometres) if it is approximately 230 000 light years across? Give your answer in scientific notation, correct to three significant figures.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Seconds in a year}&=365\times24\times60\times60\\\text{Seconds in a year}&=3.1536\times10^7\\\text{Galaxy width}&=(2.3\times10^5)(3\times10^5)(3.1536\times10^7)\text{ km}\\\text{Galaxy width}&=2.175984\times10^{18}\text{ km}\\\text{Galaxy width}&\approx2.18\times10^{18}\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far from us (in kilometres) is the farthest galaxy detected by optical telescopes if it is approximately $13\times10^9$ light years from us? Give your answer in scientific notation, correct to three significant figures.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How long does it take light to travel from the Sun to the Earth if the distance between the Sun and the Earth is $1.4951\times10^8$ km? Give your answer in minutes and seconds, correct to the nearest second.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{d}{v}\\t&=\frac{1.4951\times10^8}{3\times10^5}\text{ s}\\t&=\frac{14951}{30}\text{ s}\\t&\approx498\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

Since $498=8\times60+18$, the time is approximately 8 minutes 18 seconds.
